vts_name: Sweden Traffic (Swedish Maritime Administration TSS monitoring)
vts_boundary_basis: Ufs A (English, 15 June 2026, s.5.2.3) states the SMA monitors traffic within TSS areas, that Off Falsterborev and the Sound are monitored by Sound VTS 'while the remaining TSS areas are monitored by Sweden Traffic', and that Rule 10 violators are reported to the Swedish Transport Agency and EMSA SafeSeaNet; the Swedish Ufs A (12 May 2026) says the monitoring is AIS-based and 'utförs av centralerna SWEDEN TRAFFIC och SOUND VTS'. Decision 1 test: Sweden Traffic is not itself a statutory VTS (TSFS 2026:60 defines VTS areas only as the nine areas in annexes 1 to 9, and Ufs A lists Sweden Traffic apart from the VTS centres), but the SMA lists Sweden Traffic as one of the functions of its sjötrafikcentraler ('myndighetsövervakning av vissa havsområden') and the Stockholm centre page lists 'VTS' and 'Sweden Traffic' as co-located functions of the centre the SMA VTS directory names as 'VTS-central: Stockholm'. It is therefore shore monitoring of the TSS from a VTS centre, the same structure as Åland Sea Traffic (VTS-0043, a monitoring desk in the Western Finland VTS centre) already counted under decision 1. Category Supplemental: a monitoring/information function, not a formal VTS. Scheme-specific: no source names North Åland Sea for either Sweden Traffic or Fintraffic. Geometry (COLREG.2/Circ.60 Annex 2, WGS 84, against the 1972 Sweden-Finland shelf boundary): Part I (60°27'-60°30'N, 018°56'-019°05'E) lies wholly on the Swedish side, about 3.3 nm west of the boundary segment point 9 to point 8; in Part II (60°09'-60°12'N) the separation zone and southbound lane are on the Swedish side (zone centre about 1.2-1.3 nm west of the line point 13 to point 14) while the outer edge of the northbound lane lies up to about 1.2 nm east of it. Fintraffic states Åland Sea Traffic monitors only the Southern Åland Sea TSS, the scheme Finland 'together with Sweden' set up. The scheme is therefore predominantly in the Swedish zone and falls within the SMA's general TSS monitoring allocation, with Finland's monitoring expressly limited to the southern scheme.

reporting_authority: Irish Coast Guard: MRCC Dublin (communications also via MRSC Valentia and MRSC Malin Head); other WETREP coastal States for their sectors
reporting_boundary_basis: MSC.190(79) para 2.1: the WETREP polygon runs 56°30'N 012°W - 54°40'41"N 015°W - 50°56'45"N 015°W - 48°27'N 006°25'W, with the inner closing point 21 on the Irish east coast (52°10'N 006°22'W). At Fastnet's longitude (c. 009°36'W) the southern boundary line lies near 49°23'N, about 2° south of the TSS, so the TSS (off Fastnet Rock, c. 51°18'-51°23'N) is wholly inside. Applies only to oil tankers >600 dwt carrying heavy crude, heavy fuel oil or bitumen/tar; WETREP does not name the TSS. Pass 4: MSC.190(79) annex para 6.2.1 names 'Off Fastnet Rock' among the TSS in the WETREP area. Applies to oil tankers over 600 dwt carrying heavy grade oil.
evidence_summary: Decision 7 double-check: Decision 1 is NOT met: the Irish Coast Guard is not a VTS centre. S.I. No. 573/2010 (Irish VTMIS Regulations, as amended 2012 and 2017) separates the two functions: reg. 11(2) makes the Irish Coast Guard the monitor of compliance with IMO mandatory ships' routeing systems operated by the State, while reg. 12(3) gives monitoring of VTS participation to 'the appropriate port authority' (harbour masters designated under reg. 4(b)). Irish VTS are port services within port limits (e.g. VTS DUBLIN, Dublin Port NtM 03/2026). No Irish source designates any IRCG centre as a VTS. The supplemental category IS met: the Department of Transport IRCG page (Tier 2, modified 8 July 2025, within three years) names a monitoring responsibility for this TSS: the Coast Guard 'Monitors maritime traffic within Ireland's Traffic Separation Schemes (Tuskar/Fastnet)'. With the Tier 1 statutory duty in reg. 11(2), this is a named, current, official monitoring responsibility for the TSS, which the positive-association standard accepts, by a body that is not a VTS. So: monitoring-information service, supplemental, not core. The Fastnet TSS (separation zone centred 51 20.0 N 009 25.8 W to 51 18.2 N 009 35.2 W, Irish datum, COLREG.2/Circ.41) is about 52 NM from Roches Point, so the Port of Cork VTS is not a candidate on distance, though its port limits were not checked. | Earlier record: Inside the WETREP (VRS-0005) mandatory reporting area (tankers with heavy grade oil only). The Irish Coast Guard monitors traffic in the TSS, but no declared VTS area was found covering it.
source_date: MSC.190(79) 2004-12-06 (in force 2005-07-01); gov.ie IRCG page modified 2025-07-08; accessed 2026-09-29

evidence_summary: FC-A VTS finding: MSN 1796 Amendment 4 (SRC-2091), current and unwithdrawn per GOV.UK (SRC-2092; GOV.UK search on 30 September 2026 shows no later amendment), lists all UK VTS designated by the MCA; MGN 401 Amdt 3 (SRC-2108) makes the MCA the UK competent authority for VTS, requires a harbour authority to apply to the MCA for designation of its VTS and approval of its VTS area, and has the MCA promulgate the list of designated VTS in MSN 1796. The list contains no Holyhead or Anglesey service. The only designated VTS in the region, Liverpool (Mersey VTS), ends at the statutory Port of Liverpool limit, 003 32 W (SRC-2109, SRC-2110), about 60 nm east of the TSS. Holyhead Port Control (Stena Line Ports) is not a designated VTS; under MGN 401 para 4.2.2 a harbour authority's service is within its own port limits, which for Holyhead are the 1959 Act harbour (SRC-2113), while the TSS inner edge lies about 5.9 nm from the Holyhead breakwater and about 3 nm off the Skerries (A.161(ES.IV) centreline positions, SRC-2114). No official source states that Holyhead Port Control or HM Coastguard (Holyhead MRCC) monitors the TSS; rescue-centre watch-keeping is not a VTS centre and is not counted (project decisions, 'not changed' list). | Earlier record: Outside the WETREP polygon despite being listed in WETREP para 6.2.1 (conflict recorded). No Part I MRS. VTS coverage not established.

North of 53 33N the limit turns 065 degrees and diverges from point 11. The closest gap (about 22 m on the OSGB36 reading) is of the order of the Act's one-second longitude precision (about 18 m) and smaller than the datum ambiguity itself (about 90 m).

evidence_summary: Decision 7 double-check: Mersey VTS is the harbour authority's VTS for the Port of Liverpool, whose limit between 53 29 00N and 53 33 00N is the meridian 003 32 00W (1971 Act s.2, restated in the 2021 byelaws; no datum stated). The TSS eastern edge (Circ.60, WGS 84: 9 at 003 32.10W, 4 at 003 32.15W, 1 at 003 32.18W) is 0.059 to 0.107 nm west of the limit if read as WGS 84, and 0.012 to 0.059 nm if read as OSGB36 (the limit converts to 003 32.077W; ED50 gives 003 32.091W). North of 53 33N the limit turns 065 degrees and diverges from point 11. The closest gap (about 22 m on the OSGB36 reading) is of the order of the Act's one-second longitude precision (about 18 m) and smaller than the datum ambiguity itself (about 90 m). | Earlier record: FC-A VTS finding: The statutory Port of Liverpool is defined by the Mersey Docks and Harbour Act 1971 s.2 (SRC-2110), restated verbatim in the Port of Liverpool General Byelaws 2021, confirmed 26 March 2021 (SRC-2109), and applied by SI 2021/45 art.2 (SRC-2111): from the Redstones, Hoylake, 'to a position in latitude 53 degrees 29 minutes 00 seconds north and longitude 3 degrees 32 minutes 00 seconds west, thence in a true north direction to ... 53 degrees 33 minutes ... 3 degrees 32 minutes 00 seconds west', then 065 degrees towards Formby Point. This agrees with the 2026 Pilotage Directions '6.5mls west of the Bar Light' (SRC-2093). Boundary test against COLREG.2/Circ.60 (SRC-2096, WGS 84): the TSS eastern edge (points 9, 4, 1: 003 32.10 to 003 32.18 W between 53 29.96 and 53 32.76 N) lies west of the 003 32.00 W meridian limit; north of 53 33 N the limit turns north-east, away from point 11 (53 34.56 N 003 32.24 W). The Act's datum is not stated: taken as WGS 84 the gap is 0.06 to 0.11 nm; converted from OSGB36 the limit is 003 32.08 W (gap 0.01 to 0.06 nm); from ED50 003 32.09 W. On every reading the TSS lies wholly outside the port, its eastern edge coinciding with the port limit (Boundary only). Mersey VTS is the VTS of the Port of Liverpool (SRC-089, SRC-2095) and the harbour authority states that it provides no traffic service outside its statutory limits (NtM 70/2017, SRC-2094, still in force per NtM 1/2026 and the MDHC notices page, SRC-2112). No Peel Ports source names the Liverpool Bay TSS; the only report points are east of the Bar. | Earlier record: No Part I MRS (outside WETREP). Mersey VTS is a port VTS whose area is not shown to reach the TSS.

The regulation is made under art. 13 of Act 41/2003, which allows the minister to entrust vaktstöð siglinga with routeing management in specified areas (the Act footnotes Reg. 524/2008 there). Act 41/2003 art. 2 gives vaktstöð siglinga AIS monitoring of ships in the whole Icelandic EEZ, which contains the TSS. evidence_summary: FC-A VTS finding: Regulation 524/2008 (Annex I Part II), made under art. 13 of Act 41/2003 (routeing management may be entrusted to vaktstöð siglinga), establishes this TSS at the southern end of the outer route that all ships over 5,000 GT and all ships carrying dangerous or noxious cargo in bulk must use (arts 4 and 5); vaktstöð siglinga administers the regulation's reporting and may grant exemptions from it (art. 8). Act 41/2003 art. 2 gives vaktstöð siglinga AIS monitoring and surveillance of ships in the Icelandic EEZ; the TSS (about 63 31 N to 63 34 N, 023 29 W to 023 38 W) lies about 20 NM off Reykjanes, inside the EEZ. Geographic extent of the statutory monitoring function therefore covers the TSS (decision 1: monitoring by the VTS centre counts). Weaker than TSS-0092: no procedure names this TSS specifically. Checker: the Act 41/2003 art. 13 footnote attaches the power to entrust vaktstöð siglinga with routeing management specifically to Reg. 524/2008, which establishes this TSS (Annex I Part II), and art. 8 exemptions cover the art. 5 outer-route obligation that runs through this TSS; this is a statutory responsibility for the routeing measures that include the TSS, not proximity. | Earlier record: TRANSREP does not include this TSS (outside to the west). MTS monitors a national reporting system but is not shown to be a VTS or to cover the TSS.
unresolved_issue: Link rests on the EEZ-wide statutory monitoring duty plus the regulation that creates the TSS, not on a procedure naming this TSS. If the project requires TSS-specific wording, downgrade this record to UNRESOLVED (the service itself stays counted via TSS-0092).

vts_boundary_basis: CCS Cartagena is a SASEMAR centre that operates a contracted port maritime traffic service (STM) for the Cartagena Port Authority with VTS-trained controllers (SRC-2214, SRC-2011, SRC-2213), so it is a VTS-type centre in the same sense as CCS Almería (VTS-0202). Its only statutory service area is port waters: Zona II ends at the Punta del Sofre to Cabo Tiñoso line (SRC-2218); recomputed, vertex L-2 (37 33.5 N 000 57.3 W, ED50 UTM converted) lies 17.1 NM from the nearest TSS vertex, and about 12 NM even if the inshore zone is carried to the coast at Cabo de Palos; the ED50 to WGS84 shift is about 0.1 NM, so the port area clearly does not reach the TSS. The link therefore rests on monitoring by a VTS centre (decision 1): a Government Delegation statement, reported in September 2024 (SRC-2125), that CCS Cartagena detected a vessel contravening the Cabo de Palos DST, called it on VHF 16, and that the Capitanía opened sanction proceedings; Tramos (SRC-096), an official ministry publication written by SASEMAR, lists Cabo de Palos among Spain's DST and says the DST are controlled by the STM/VTS function assigned to SASEMAR; RD 210/2004 (SRC-2215) gives the CCS a general duty to follow ships using IMO routeing systems.

tss_name: Saronicos Gulf (in the approaches to Piraeus Harbour)
vts_boundary_basis: Service existence is current and official: the 24/25 Sept 2026 Diavgeia decision (re-read from the page image) lists Piraeus among seven existing HCG VTS centres, each responsible for a defined area of responsibility. The link rests on P.D. 81/2014 (official FEK, in force), which provides that the Saronikos Port Office, whose district covers the Attica coast beside the scheme, does not exercise vessel traffic control in 'the defined traffic separation zone of the port of Piraeus'. The only IMO scheme in the approaches to Piraeus is TSS-0111, whose IMO title is 'in the approaches to Piraeus Harbour' (separation zone from about 6 nm to 17 nm south of the harbour), and the vessel traffic control function of the Piraeus authority is exercised through VTS Piraeus. NGA Pub. 132 (2026, lead only) independently states that a VTS 'is established in the approaches to Piraievs'. The 2003 VTMIS regulation defines areas in annexes, but its published annexes cover only the Ionian centres, so no official Piraeus polygon exists to test. No official source places the scheme outside VTS Piraeus.

vts_name: Suez Canal Vessel Traffic Management System (SC-VTMS), Port Said approaches
vts_boundary_basis: Reopened SCA Rules of Navigation (Dec 2020 edition, still the published edition): SC-VTMS gives radar, AIS and camera surveillance and tracking 'throughout the Canal and its approaches at Port Said', from vessels 'arriving at SC approaches (15 miles faraway) until anchorage in the waiting areas', feeding the SCA Port Said port management control centre (SRC-2236). The IMO schemes are themselves titled 'approaches to Bur Said'. No SCA boundary polygon exists, so the 15 miles was recomputed (WGS 84 TSS coordinates, SRC-2239; spherical distances, error under 0.5%) from every reference point SCA itself uses: Fairway Buoy (SRC-2237): points 19, 15, 16, 17 at 12.3, 12.5, 12.6, 12.8 nm, about 2.3 to 2.7 nm of each lane inside; Northern anchorage Zone One NW corner: 5.4 to 5.6 nm; Zone Two NW corner: 7.0 to 7.9 nm; East Channel Hm 230 buoy: 10.9 to 11.5 nm. The NW end (points 13, 14, 18, 20) is 22 to 29 nm out on any reading, so Partial. Only a harbour-entrance reference (about 31°16'N 32°19'E, not used by SCA for this purpose) puts the TSS outside (16.3 nm). NGA Pub. 132 (corrected March 2026, lead) independently states that 'traffic surveillance of the canal and port approaches is maintained by radar' (SRC-2238). Decision 4 was not the only obstacle before, but the remaining obstacles are interpretation (reference point, unnamed TSS) rather than contrary evidence: no official source places the SC-VTMS limit short of the TSS.

tss_name: In the approaches to Ras Tanura and Ju’aymah
vts_name: Ras Tanura Vessel Traffic Management System (Ras Tanura VTMS)
vts_authority: Saudi Aramco (Manager, Port Operations, Port of Ras Tanura)
vts_centre: Ras Tanura Port Control (Ras Tanura Port Control Center)
vts_boundary_basis: Aramco July 2025 book: the VTMS is mandatory 'for all vessels within the Port of Ras Tanura'. The 11-point harbour boundary has its eastern limit on 50 23 E between 27 00 N and 27 12 N. The IMO scheme (A.338(IX) as amended) runs from 50 42 E west to the Ras Tanura channel at about 26 41 N 50 12 E. The Ju'aymah departure lane (Part III) runs east along 27 11.5 N to 50 36 E. Inside the port limits: the channel section, the Ju'aymah approach lane and the western end of the departure lane. Outside them: the eastern approach lanes (about 50 23 E to 50 42 E) and the eastern part of the Ju'aymah departure lane (50 23 E to 50 36 E). Pub. 172 (2025) lists VTMS reporting to Ras Tannurah Port Control from Ras Tannurah Lighted Buoy (27 06 N 50 57 E), east of the scheme, and the Aramco speed rules apply to all ships 'using the Ras Tanura Port, Traffic Separation Scheme' from the Approach Buoy. So traffic in the whole scheme is in contact with the service. The service's defined area is still the port. Hence partial. The service is a VTS in its own right: it is a mandatory VTMS with a 'VTS Operator' information service, so the decision 5 fallback is not needed.
reporting_boundary_basis: Not in IMO Part I. Reports to Ras Tanura Port Control (Entry buoy, A buoy, anchoring, departure) are routine VTMS reporting and form part of the VTS, not a separate MRS. No national mandatory reporting scheme found in Pub. 172 (2025) or the Aramco book.
evidence_summary: Aramco's July 2025 port book describes a mandatory VTMS with a 'VTS Operator' information service. It covers all vessels within the Port of Ras Tanura and states that the Ras Tanura Channel separation zones and routes are IMO-approved. Speed and reporting rules apply to 'all ships using the Ras Tanura Port, Traffic Separation Scheme'. The port boundary includes the channel and Ju'aymah parts of the TSS but not the eastern approach lanes between about 50 23 E and 50 42 E. Pub. 172 (2025) confirms the VTMS covers Ras Tannurah and the Ju Aymah terminals and lists reporting points along the approach. It is an official port traffic management service (decision 5), with partial coverage.
source_date: Aramco Ports and Terminals July 2025; NGA Pub. 172 24th ed. 2025; IMO A.338(IX) 1975
unresolved_issue: The current IMO 2025 geometry has not been checked against A.338(IX) (1975, 'as amended'); later amendments may move the eastern end. VTMS coverage of the eastern lanes beyond the port limit rests only on reporting points, not on a defined service area.

vts_boundary_basis: Geometry recomputed. A 2026 report (SRC-2259) says precautionary area No. 2 connects with the East Lamma Channel TSS section. Official Guangdong MSA material, 6 March 2025 (SRC-2260, 'Guangdong Maritime' government account, article supplied by Guangzhou MSA), is about the Dangan Channel TSS. It illustrates the TSS waters with a 'Guangzhou MSA VTS radar screenshot' ('广州海事局VTS雷达截图') of fishing vessels in the area. It tells ships to strengthen contact with the VTS and, in emergencies, to call Guangzhou VTS on VHF 08/09. That is shore monitoring of the TSS by a VTS centre, which counts under decision 1. source_date: 2026-04-08 (news report); Guangzhou VTS guide undated
unresolved_issue: Conflict (included by default): The TSS lies exactly on the HKSAR boundary, with the same datum and coincident coordinates. The HK VTS boundary therefore neither clearly includes nor clearly excludes it. The official HK MD 2003 paper says parts of the scheme lie inside Hong Kong waters and are served by the HK VTC. The adopted 2018 IMO geometry puts the scheme's northern edge on the boundary line rather than across it. Both readings have official support. Flag INCLUDED_BY_DEFAULT_ON_CONFLICT. This splices FC-B's VTS-0028 finding into the register, but at Boundary only, not Partial. The formal Guangzhou VTS area, per the service guide reproduced by a third party (V-S12), has outer line L1 meeting the Dangan waterway at 22°08'54.5"N 113°57'30"E. That is about 8 nm west of the TSS's western part (about 114°06'E per FC-B) and about 13 nm west of precautionary area No. 2 (114°11'.77E). The 2026 report itself says key ships bound for Hong Kong were previously outside VTS coverage, and the Dangan station is in trial, not formal, operation. Against that, the official 2025 MSA material shows Guangzhou VTS radar imaging the TSS waters and directs TSS traffic to Guangzhou VTS. Official material shows monitoring while the defined area does not reach the TSS. Flag INCLUDED_BY_DEFAULT_ON_CONFLICT. The full COLREG.2/Circ.71 annex was not retrieved (the ics.org.ir copy failed), so the lane edges west and east of precautionary area No. 2 were not tested against the boundary. Only precautionary area No. 2 was plotted. If a lane edge crosses north of 22°08'54.5"N, coverage would become Partial and the outcome INCLUDE. No MSA navigation notice or VTS area announcement extending the Guangzhou VTS area (or defining a Dangan sector) was found, and there is no confirmation that trial operation has become formal operation. The mainland and HK parts sit on either side of the HKSAR boundary. This record takes no view on jurisdiction beyond the published boundary. Shenzhen VTS remains excluded (line L7 about 22°24'.8N, over 15 nm north, per FC-B).

reporting_scheme_name: MASTREP (Modernised Australian Ship Tracking and Reporting System), national mandatory scheme under the Navigation Act 2012 and Marine Order 63 (Vessel reporting systems) 2019; not an IMO Part I system
reporting_authority: AMSA (JRCC Australia)
reporting_boundary_basis: MASTREP area is the Australian SRR for which RCC Australia is responsible (V-S16); the TSS lies in Australian coastal waters well inside the SRR. Mandatory only for foreign vessels between first arrival at and final departure from an Australian port, and for regulated Australian vessels in the MASTREP area (V-S15), so through-transiting foreign ships are outside it. Automatic AIS-based reporting. Pass 4: Marine Order 63 (2019) gives effect to SOLAS V/11 (s.2), applies to regulated Australian vessels and to foreign vessels from arrival at their first Australian port until departure from their final Australian port (s.6(1)), with a strict-liability penalty (s.7). Counted as MRS under the project rule that a national scheme counts when it imposes a penal reporting duty on foreign ships in the TSS under defined voyage conditions. Through traffic not calling at Australian ports is not covered.

vts_boundary_basis: No official source describes a VTS whose area includes Part 1. The Panama Canal Authority's Flamenco Signal Station coordinates Pacific anchorage and harbour movements (N-2-2026) and is called a signal station, not a VTS; N-2-2026 does not name the TSS or define a service area.
reporting_boundary_basis: No IMO Part I system applies (Part I inventory lists only GALREP, VRS-0019, in this region, confined to the Galapagos). COLREG.2/Circ.65, AMP MMC-304 and AMP Circular DGPIMA-005-DECCP-2026 attach no reporting requirement to the TSS. The ACP call to Flamenco Signal Station at 8 nm from the Pacific Sea Buoy (about 11 nm from Flamenco Island) is canal and anchorage arrival reporting, not a separate MRS. Geographically it falls near the northern (inner) end of the lanes (08°44.7'N to 08°46'N), but the buoy position was not verified from an official source.
evidence_summary: Decision 7 double-check: The Cristobal test gives the same result on the Pacific side, and the geometry is slightly stronger. ACP N-2-2026 (1 Jan 2026, Tier 2) para 2 makes Flamenco Signal Station a traffic-control function. It coordinates anchorage entry and exit and harbour movements, recommends anchoring positions, gives masters the expected traffic movements at 2 nm from the Pacific Sea Buoy, and checks anchored positions by radar. Vessels must call it 8 nm from the Pacific Sea Buoy, 'about 11 Nautical Miles from Flamenco Island'. The Sea Buoy is at 8°51'45"N 79°29'50"W (ACP Navigation Regulation art. 37.3; NGA Pub. 153 gives 79°29'49.8"W, the same position to 0.003 nm). Recomputed on WGS 84 (Vincenty) from COLREG.2/Circ.65 Annex 1 Part 1: the four northern (inner) end points of the scheme lie 7.56 nm (point 4), 7.66 nm (9), 7.71 nm (10) and 7.92 nm (3) from the Sea Buoy. They also lie 10.96-11.34 nm from Flamenco Island (8°55'N 79°31'W, whole-minute NGA position). So the whole inner edge of the TSS is inside the mandatory 8 nm call ring, and the ring crosses the southbound lane, separation zone and northbound lane 0.08-0.46 nm south of the inner ends. ACP's own 'about 11 nm from Flamenco Island' gloss puts the call point at the inner end of the scheme. The southern 49-50 nm of Part 1 (to 7°45'N) is outside the ring. NGA Pub. 153 puts the reporting sequence under the heading 'Vessel Traffic Management System (VTMS)'. Arrivals report passing the latitude of Punta Mala (7°28'N, south of the whole of Part 1), then report to Flamenco on arrival. The ACP Regulation (art. 30) also asks for the Punta Mala passing time. For Cristobal the call ring passed through the inner end (lane end at 8.02 nm). Here all inner points are 0.08-0.44 nm inside the ring, so the same test applies, with a comparable margin. | Earlier record: IMO B-VIII/1 Part 1, adopted MSC 93 (COLREG.2/Circ.65), in force 1 Dec 2014. Current ACP (A-24-2026) and AMP (DGPIMA-005-DECCP-2026) notices refer to the TSS only for the seasonal 10 kn whale recommendation. ACP N-2-2026 requires a VHF Ch 12 call to Flamenco Signal Station 8 nm from the Pacific Sea Buoy. That is canal arrival coordination and does not show a VTS covering the TSS. No Part I MRS. No official source shows VTS coverage, and no official complete list of Panamanian VTS shows that there is none.
unresolved_issue: Conflict (included by default): The official sources disagree on extent and character, as they did for TSS-0213. (a) Supporting the link: ACP N-2-2026 requires the Flamenco call, and has Flamenco begin anchorage allocation and traffic coordination, at 8 nm from the Sea Buoy. That point falls on the inner end of the TSS (inner points 7.56-7.92 nm from the buoy; the ring is 0.08-0.46 nm down the lanes). NGA Pub. 153 describes this reporting chain, starting south of the TSS at Punta Mala, as the Panama Canal VTMS. NGA Pub. 148 says the same VTMS 'covers the approaches to Colon'. (b) Against the link: ACP calls Flamenco a signal station, not a VTS, and states no service area or radar coverage. The Canal operating area is described as 'the Pacific entrance and its anchorage areas'. The southernmost anchorage limit (8°49'55"N, art. 37.3.b) is 5.05-5.89 nm north of the TSS inner points. ACP N-1-2026 para 32.d treats Canal waters as beginning no further out than 3 nm from the Sea Buoy, which puts the TSS 4.6-4.9 nm outside them. The 8 nm call is a reporting point, not a stated control boundary. (c) The margin (0.08-0.44 nm) is small relative to the imprecision of an 8 nm call ring measured from a floating buoy, and the 'about 11 nm from Flamenco' gloss. So whether ACP traffic control reaches the TSS depends on which reading is taken. Official sources support either reading, so decision 7 applies. Classed as Supplemental (traffic control, not a formal VTS), with coverage limited to the inner end. Flag INCLUDED_BY_DEFAULT_ON_CONFLICT. Service identity: recommend recording ONE Canal-wide ACP service, with two signal stations, for TSS-0213 and TSS-0176, not two services. The D8 new_services entry ('ACP Cristobal Signal Station / Panama Canal Marine Traffic Control (Atlantic entrance)') should be renamed and widened to cover both stations and both TSS, so TSS-0176 adds no further service. If the project instead counts each signal station as its own service, TSS-0176 becomes +1 supplemental. No ACP statement of Flamenco radar or AIS coverage extent, and no service polygon, was found. ACP N-2-2026 mentions radar only for checking anchored positions. The ACP Navigation Regulation was read from a third-party compiled copy (ARMCOL), which may predate recent amendments; the official Acuerdo 360 scan on pancanal.com is not machine-readable. The ACP A-24-2026 and AMP DGPIMA-005-DECCP-2026 whale-speed notices, cited in the master record, were not reopened. Flamenco Island's position is to the whole minute only.

vts_name: VTS Callao (Servicio de Control del Tráfico Marítimo, TRAMAR, Callao)
vts_boundary_basis: Official Peruvian sources now support the link, so NGA is no longer needed to close it; NGA stays only as corroboration, consistent with the Chilean standard. (1) Tier 1: the consolidated Reglamento of D.L. 1147 (D.S. 015-2014-DE as amended to D.S. 001-2024-DE, published by DICAPI) establishes TRAMAR as the National Maritime Authority's Maritime Traffic Control Service, operated through the harbour master 24 hours a day. It can interact with ships and respond to traffic in the area under control. Its functions include monitoring and controlling maritime traffic and ordering ship movements (arts. 159-171). Ships must notify TRAMAR on entering the control area 20 nm from the first or outer channel buoys, report again at 4 nm 'para recibir instrucciones', and report outbound at 4 and 20 nm (arts. 164, 170). (2) Tier 2: MTC (15 Sep 2024) and the Marina de Guerra del Perú (19 Sep 2024) confirm that the Callao Maritime Traffic Control Centre was re-equipped and inaugurated as 'VTS Callao'. It is administered by DICAPI, with three coastal radars and seven optronic cameras. (3) Geometry: every point of all three Callao TSS parts lies within 3.7 nm of position (24) 12°02.05'S 077°14.64'W (WGS 84), the precautionary area and ATBA at the outer fairway approach (NGA gives the traffic circle at 12°01.8'S 77°14.8'W, 0.3 nm away). The whole scheme therefore lies inside the 20 nm control-area notice and inside the 4 nm instruction report, with a margin of more than 16 nm to the notice limit. NGA Pub. 125 (lead) names the scheme 'TSS (TRAMAR)' and requires reports at 20, 10 and 4 miles and at the Outer Fairway Lighted Buoy. The service qualifies as core: it is designated VTS by the operating authority, and under decision 5 it is also an official traffic control service whose control area demonstrably contains the TSS.

Baseline/internal-waters status not established. Counted under decision 3a. evidence_summary: Decision 7 double-check: This is not a boundary question: the TSS is inside the harbour master's jurisdiction. The question is whether the candidate is a VTS, a port traffic centre or a monitoring/information service at all. The current official operating conditions for Bahía de Concepción (C.P. Talcahuano Ord. 12.600/491, 26 Dec 2023, Tier 2, under three years old) name the Boca Grande TSS and give its coordinates. They set out the complete arrangements for the bay: arrivals and departures coordinated by ship agencies through the online platform, pilotage, anchorage allocation by e-mail, an anchoring report to 'Talcahuano Capuerto Radio', and VHF 16 contact with the local maritime authority. They establish no VTS, traffic control centre, monitoring area or traffic-organisation function, and do not require reports when using or approaching the TSS. That is an authority source stating the relevant scope, which meets the negative standard. DIRECTEMAR's operational information page names the Chilean traffic control stations it uses (Punta Delgada 'VTS Básico', Bahía Félix, Paso Tortuoso, Evangelistas, Puerto Williams) and none at Talcahuano. The same standard as for Chile's other TSS was applied. NGA Pub. 125 was accepted for Arica, Iquique, Quintero and Valparaíso because it describes a named VTS with a boundary diagram or coordinates. For Talcahuano, the same volume lists only a VHF 16 'information service' under 'Signals' at the Port Authority building, with no name, area or traffic function. The same volume therefore does not support a VTS here. Per the project note, harbour-master radio contact and monitoring by bodies that are not VTS centres remain leads, and a radio contact point alone is not a VTS. | Earlier record: Recorded project decision 3a counts CHILREP with its flag/internal-water qualifications. CHILREP (national, Chile; mandatory for Chilean-flag ships and for foreign ships in internal waters). Whether the Talcahuano information service is a VTS; whether the TSS lies in internal waters (CHILREP position-report duty).

tss_name: At the approaches to Puerto Cristobal
vts_boundary_basis: No official source defines a VTS area that includes this TSS. Under ACP N-2-2026 (Z2-S6), Cristobal Signal Station coordinates anchorage entry/exit and harbour movements, and vessels must call it at 8 NM from the Atlantic Breakwater. N-2-2026 does not name the TSS or call the station a VTS. ACP's Enhanced Vessel Traffic Management System (Z2-S7) is a scheduling and information database with no stated service area. NGA Pub. 148 (Z2-S8, Tier 3) says the Panama Canal VTMS 'covers the approaches to Colon and its terminals' but gives no boundary. Coverage of the TSS lanes (about 09°28'N to 09°43'N) is not established.
reporting_boundary_basis: No IMO Part I system applies (the only Part I system in the region is GALREP, VRS-0019). COLREG.2/Circ.65 Annex 2 attaches no reporting. ACP N-2-2026 requires a VHF Ch 12 call to Cristobal Signal Station at 8 NM from the Atlantic Breakwater, plus a continuous Ch 12 watch (vessels of 300 GT or more, 100 GT or more with passengers for hire, commercial towing vessels of 8 m or more) until an ACP pilot takes control. That is canal and anchorage arrival reporting, not a separate MRS. The call point lies about 8 NM north of the breakwater, near the inner (southern) end of the TSS, where the inner lane points are at 09°31'N to 09°32.7'N. The breakwater position is not from an official source. NGA Pub. 148 gives different call distances (6 NM and 12 NM), but the current ACP notice takes precedence.
evidence_summary: Decision 7 double-check: ACP N-2-2026 (1 Jan 2026, Tier 2) makes Cristobal Signal Station a traffic-control function. It coordinates anchorage entry and exit and harbour movements, sequences and authorises all movements through the breakwater and in Limon Bay, and gives vessels a detailed account of traffic. Vessels must call it 8 nm from the Atlantic Breakwater, and it calls any vessel that has not reported by 5 nm. Recomputed on WGS 84 from Circ.65 (breakwater entrance 9°23'19"N 79°55'04"W): the inner end of the TSS lies 6.9 nm (point 2, west separation line/ITZ) to 11.2 nm (point 13) from the breakwater. The lane end at point (5) is 8.02 nm away, so the 8 nm call ring passes through the inner end of the scheme, while the outer ends reach 25.3 nm. NGA Pub. 148 says the Panama Canal VTMS 'covers the approaches to Colon and its terminals', and the TSS is the IMO scheme 'At the approaches to Puerto Cristobal'. | Earlier record: IMO B-IX/19, adopted by COLREG.2/Circ.65 (MSC 93) and implemented 1 Dec 2014, with inshore traffic zones on both sides. ACP N-2-2026 (1 Jan 2026) makes Cristobal Signal Station the point of contact at 8 NM from the Atlantic Breakwater and has it coordinate anchorage and harbour movements. It is called a signal station, not a VTS, and the notice does not refer to the TSS. NGA Pub. 148 describes a Panama Canal VTMS 'covering the approaches to Colon' without limits. No Part I MRS applies, and the ACP arrival call is canal arrival reporting. This matches the project treatment of TSS-0176 (Gulf of Panama, Flamenco Signal Station).
source_date: COLREG.2/Circ.65 23 May 2014; ACP N-2-2026 and N-3-2026 1 Jan 2026; NGA Pub. 148 19th Ed 2025 (updated 4 Sep 2026)
unresolved_issue: Conflict (included by default): The sources disagree on both characterisation and extent. (a) NGA Pub. 148 says the Panama Canal VTMS covers the approaches to Colón, which on a plain reading includes the IMO 'approaches to Puerto Cristobal' TSS. NGA is the same volume type relied on for the Chilean VTS links. (b) ACP's own texts call the unit a signal station, not a VTS, and give no service area. They define the Canal operating areas as the Atlantic entrance and its anchorage areas; the outer anchorage and sea buoy end at 9°26'20"N, 1.7-5 nm south of the TSS's inner ends. (c) The ACP mandatory call point (8 nm from the breakwater in N-2-2026, against 6 miles in the Navigation Regulation art. 36 and 12 miles in NGA) falls on the inner end of the TSS, within the imprecision of an 'Atlantic Breakwater' reference whose two heads are 0.3 nm apart. So whether ACP traffic control reaches the TSS depends on which of these readings is taken. Official sources support either reading, so decision 7 applies. Classed as Supplemental (traffic control, not a formal VTS), with coverage limited to the inner end. Flag INCLUDED_BY_DEFAULT_ON_CONFLICT. No ACP statement of VTMS radar/AIS coverage or a service polygon was found. The official Acuerdo 360 text on pancanal.com is a scanned image and could not be read (no OCR available); the compiled regulation copy is a third-party host and may predate recent amendments. ACP N-1-2026 was not retrieved. The same reasoning should be applied to TSS-0176 (Flamenco Signal Station, Pacific entrance) for consistency; that TSS was not re-examined here.

vts_boundary_basis: Overlay done on Directive 1226-r Scheme No. 3 (taken as B-X/5: same name pair, and Pub. 155 places the IMO scheme off Mys Ostrovnoy for vessels approaching Nakhodka, with a foreign-ship restriction matching the 1226-r warning). Part I lies wholly within statutory Sector 1B (separation zone 2.0-4.0 NM inside the territorial sea, 13.7-18.7 NM west of 133°43'E) and outside the operator's no-service area: about 97% of Part I with its lanes is in 1B and served. Part II: 82% of the separation zone is inside statutory 1B. The eastern end runs 2.0-2.8 NM east of 133°43'E, and about 68% lies inside Rosmorport's declared no-service coastal area Povorotny-Ostrovnoy. Only about 15% of the zone (27% with lanes) is both in 1B and served. Part III: the separation zone lies about 99.8% beyond the 12 NM limit (vertices 0.1-8.1 NM outside), so only the northern lane (about 22%) is covered. Overall: about 44% of the scheme area with lanes is in statutory 1B and about 26% is in 1B and served. There is a clear positive overlap in 2026-current official instruments (SRC-2280, SRC-2282, SRC-2283) and on the operator page (SRC-2284). Result: Partial.

vts_name: Salvamento Marítimo traffic service for the Canarias Oriental DST (CCS Las Palmas)
vts_boundary_basis: Same standard as VTS-0202 (CCS Almería, Cabo de Gata). The SASEMAR Plan Anual 2025 (SRC-2213) assigns CCS Las Palmas the task of supervising maritime traffic in the Canarias Oriental (between Gran Canaria and Fuerteventura) DST, in the same sentence and on the same footing as Finisterre, Tarifa and Almería; SASEMAR's live service page (SRC-2022) and Tramos Feb and Jul-Aug 2025 (SRC-096, SRC-2011) name Canarias Oriental and Occidental among the DST where SASEMAR monitors and assists traffic and state this is the STM/VTS function assigned to SASEMAR. The Cabo de Gata test is met: CCS controllers hold VTS certification and the CCS run VTS display systems (SRC-2213 actions 66 and TELECO), and the Canary centres also control port entries and departures (2025 figures, SRC-2221, lead). The IMO scheme text names the same centre for voluntary TSS notification (SRC-2216, Tier 1). Current operation in 2025 is reported (SRC-2221). A named monitoring responsibility for the TSS is a positive-association criterion in its own right, so no geometry turns on it.
reporting_scheme_name: CANREP (Mandatory ship reporting system for the Canary Islands)
reporting_authority: Salvamento Marítimo: MRCC Las Palmas (entry east of 015°30'W) / MRCC Tenerife (entry west of 015°30'W)
reporting_boundary_basis: CANREP area is a polygon (points A-N) along the outer limit of the territorial sea around the archipelago (MSC.213(81) para 2.1). Plotting the COLREG.2/Circ.57 coordinates shows all Eastern TSS points inside the polygon; its northern termination (points 3 and 11-12 at about 28°20'N, on the line CANREP D-E) lies on the CANREP boundary line within 0.05', and the polygon vertex used for the TSS's inshore traffic zone coincides with a CANREP vertex, so the TSS lies within the reporting area. Applies only to tankers of 600 dwt and above carrying heavy crude, heavy fuel oil, bitumen or tar.
